questions.q: How many passengers, including Passepartout, had disappeared after the attack?
choices: Two
Three
Five
Ten
questions.evidence: Three passengers including Passepartout had disappeared.

questions.q: How had Phileas Fogg come through the fight?
choices: He had hurt his arm very badly
He had not received a scratch
He had a deep cut on his head
He had twisted his ankle

questions.q: What did Mr. Fogg tell Aouda he would do about Passepartout?
choices: Wait at the station until the soldiers found him
Find him, living or dead
Send a telegraph to the police in Omaha
Offer a reward to anyone who brought him back
questions.evidence: I will find him, living or dead

questions.q: Why did going after Passepartout mean Fogg was probably giving up his bet?
choices: The soldiers would charge him all his money
A day's delay would make him miss the New York steamer
He would have to give his carpet-bag to the captain
The rules of the bet said he must never leave the train
questions.evidence: The delay of a single day would make him lose the steamer at New York

questions.q: Why did the captain at first not want to chase the Sioux?
choices: His soldiers had no horses or guns that day
He could not leave the fort unprotected
He did not believe anyone was really missing
He was waiting for orders from Washington
questions.evidence: I cannot leave the fort unprotected

choices: Aouda offered him all the money in the carpet-bag
Fogg said he would go alone, and the captain was touched
Fix showed the captain his police warrant
A telegram arrived ordering him to send help

questions.q: What did Mr. Fogg ask Fix to do while he was gone?
choices: Go along to guard the sergeant's men
Stay behind at the station with Aouda
Ride ahead to the next station
Watch over the wounded colonel

questions.q: What did Mr. Fogg promise the soldiers if they saved the prisoners?
choices: A free trip to England on his steamer
Five thousand dollars to divide among them
A silver medal from the Queen for every man
A great dinner at the best hotel in Omaha
questions.evidence: I will divide five thousand dollars among you

questions.q: How did Fix feel soon after Fogg left?
choices: Relieved that he could finally rest
Angry at himself for letting Fogg go alone
Proud that he had kept his promise to Aouda
Happy because the reward would soon be his

questions.q: Under new snow, every footprint "would be effaced." What does effaced mean?
choices: Wiped out
Made deeper
Frozen hard
Made easier to see

questions.q: What came out of the mist from the east at about two o'clock?
choices: A rescue train sent from Omaha
The runaway locomotive, coming back
A wagon carrying more soldiers
Fogg leading the three rescued travellers
questions.evidence: The locomotive, which was slowly approaching with deafening whistles

questions.q: What did Aouda decide when the conductor said the train would start at once?
choices: She would go on and wait for Fogg in New York
She would not go, but would stay and wait
She would beg the colonel to make it wait
She would ride back to the fort with Fix

questions.q: Fix had planned to leave, but did not get on the train. What does this show?
choices: He was too badly wounded to walk
He still wished to struggle on to the end
He had lost his ticket during the attack
He was afraid the Sioux would attack again
questions.evidence: He wished to struggle on to the end.

questions.q: What did Aouda do through the long, cold night?
choices: She slept in the waiting-room beside the stove
She wandered at the edge of the plains, full of worry
She sat talking with Fix on the station bench
She wrote a letter to Mr. Fogg's friends in London
questions.evidence: wandered about on the verge of the plains

questions.q: What had Passepartout and the other prisoners begun to do just before the soldiers arrived?
choices: Struggle with their captors
Hide in a deep snowy ravine
Light a fire to send a signal
Run back toward the railroad
questions.evidence: had begun to struggle with their captors

questions.q: Which title best fits what this chapter is mostly about?
choices: Fogg gives up his time and money to rescue his servant
Fix finally arrests Fogg at a lonely fort in the snow
Aouda goes on alone to New York to wait for her friends
Colonel Proctor and Fogg settle their quarrel at last
questions.evidence: He had sacrificed his fortune, and was now risking his life, all without hesitation, from duty
